query: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes June 24 confirmed death toll latest figures, trajectory of confirmed deaths reported by authorities and Wikipedia, number of missing persons and rescue operation status
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on the June 24, 2026 Venezuela earthquakes:

**Confirmed death toll trajectory (steeply rising):**
- June 24–25: ~188–235 dead
- June 29: **1,719** (UN, per Venezuelan authorities)
- July 7: **3,535** (Al Jazeera)
- As of July 2026: **more than 5,200** (Wikipedia — latest aggregate)

The toll roughly doubled each reporting interval, and every source emphasized it "continues to climb" as teams reach isolated/damaged areas. USGS PAGER projected the eventual total could exceed 10,000.

**Missing persons:** No precise official count at any stage; latest figure is described as "multiple tens of thousands still missing."

**Rescue operations:** Active — 2,000+ workers from 27 countries and 160+ search dogs deployed by June 29, extending beyond the 72-hour window. By July 7, the effort shifted toward humanitarian crisis management (17,854 unhoused, ~12,800 in 80 shelters), with analysts criticizing the slow state response.

Full structured findings (key facts, dated data points, and all sources) have been submitted via the StructuredOutput tool.

key_facts: Two earthquakes (Mw 7.2 foreshock + Mw 7.5 mainshock) struck northwestern/central Venezuela on 24 June 2026 at 18:04 VET, 39 seconds apart, with epicenters in Veroes Municipality, Yaracuy.
Confirmed death toll rose from ~188-235 (June 24-25) to 1,719 (June 29) to 3,535 (July 7) to more than 5,200 (as of July 2026 per Wikipedia).
Injured figures rose from ~1,520-4,300 initially to ~5,000 (June 29) to 16,740 (July 7); Wikipedia lists 16,700 as of July 2026.
Missing persons: no precise official count confirmed; latest description is 'multiple tens of thousands still remain missing.'
USGS PAGER modeling projected the death toll could exceed 10,000, with early casualty ranges cited between 10,000 and 100,000.
Rescue operation was active: 2,000+ workers from 27 countries, 160+ search dogs, 40+ teams as of June 29; survivors pulled beyond 72-hour window.
La Guaira state saw ~80% of buildings collapse; roughly 60,000 buildings damaged/destroyed nationwide.
By July 7, focus shifted to humanitarian crisis: 17,854 unhoused, ~12,800 in 80 shelters in Caracas/La Guaira; health-crisis warnings.
The mainshock was the strongest earthquake in Venezuela since the 1900 San Narciso earthquake.
~500 aftershocks (including a M5.2) and tropical weather complicated recovery efforts.
